audit: failure-mode audit of the mechanisms recorded as eliminated
method: one agent per loop read source+output and classified the failure mode; a second, adversarial agent re-read the same files and tried to refute the classification; an independent simulation measured what the sample sizes could detect

headline.statement: of six mechanisms recorded as eliminated, one is genuinely absent, one is null only once abundance is controlled, one was an annotation-depth artifact, one was never tested because its control arm could not fail, one is diluted but real inside its own population, and one shows real signal the moment a rate replaces an annotation bit

revised_status.121_degron_motifs: GENUINELY ABSENT for the protein-only oscillators; instrument validated on a contemporaneous positive control (KEN AUC 0.6899 inside 'both'), well-powered flanking comparison 14.8% vs 12.3% with MDE 6.3pp against a 37.1pp reference. Scope: licenses 'the APC/C linear-degron signature is absent', NOT 'b(t) regulation is absent'. The declared gate was separately broken: simulated power 0.0% for D-box and D-box+, and the n=38 comparator was itself degron-enriched so the gate pointed backwards.
revised_status.118_relocalisation: NOT A NULL RESULT AT ALL -- the loop never tested oscillation (n_pos=0, n_neg=0, zero cell-cycle references in 321 log lines). When the omitted contrast is run: 461 vs 8008, cytosolic pool AUC 0.5378 unmatched -> 0.5214 abundance-matched. The apparent effect is a detection gradient: pulsed proteins carry 2.3x the copies (AUC 0.613, p=3e-16). Q4's acceptance window contained the null's entire +/-4sd span, so all 20 shuffles passed it.
revised_status.137_ubiquitin_annotation: WRONG PROPERTY, upheld. The static bit marks 24% of the proteome so binary AUC is capped at 0.574 even at OR 2.0. Swapping it for the measured rate k_deg_per_h separates the sets at AUC 0.5704, p=0.0164, t_half 60.4h vs 78.2h, surviving publication-quintile matching. ALSO: U5 was an unearned PASS -- it promised a computation with the model's measured b, printed hypothetical half-lives instead, and set the gate True unconditionally. The promised number is 0.0-0.7%.
revised_status.145_phosphodegrons_naive: ANNOTATION-DEPTH ARTIFACT, not biology. Degron 'occupancy' is a near-monotone function of curated phosphosite count (2.1% -> 60.0% across site bins, rho +0.227), and the groups differ in exactly that (median 8/4/3 sites, matching the raw rate order 22.9/14.6/10.7%). Matched: OR 1.57 -> 1.02, permutation p=0.227. A site-placement null gives identical enrichment in all four groups and the direction flips. Also power-limited: ~0.07 for a realistic effect.
revised_status.146_phosphodegrons_ELM: INERT NULL -- THE MECHANISM WAS NEVER TESTED. For a binary score AUC=(1+q-f)/2, so the maximum attainable gain for the PHOSPHO-CAPABLE control arm was +0.01619 mean against a +0.02000 bar: no assignment of phosphosites to any gene could have made the control violate its falsification condition. Meanwhile the effect IS there and large: 4/5 FBW7 and 10/15 TRCP1 curated substrates phospho-occupied = 14/20 = 70.0% vs 2.92% background, 24-fold, TRCP1 Fisher p=6.11e-17, with a monotone arm gradient REQUIRED 70.0% > CAPABLE 30.0% > INCAPABLE 8.9% (p=1.2e-06). Q3 reported this as -0.0841 because gain = AUC(binary sub-indicator) - AUC(graded superset), and the REQUIRED arm's acceptance region was 2 of 96 discrete outcome cells -- it measured UniProt annotation completeness for twenty proteins, not the mechanism.
revised_status.153_dbox_quality: SIGNAL-DILUTED, upheld and strengthened by a leave-substrates-out test nobody had run: APC substrates among oscillators score AUC 0.6564 vs flat while all other oscillators score 0.5134 -- 71% of the excess from 17.3% of the positives, surviving pubs-matched (p=0.0215) and pubs+length-matched (p=0.0115) nulls. Fame falsifier: the 18 MOST famous non-APC oscillators give 0.5315. Corrections to loop 153: the gate ceiling was 0.5865 against a 0.60 gate (unreachable); the +50.6% baseline was wrong (+28.8% against the right comparator, so predicted +4.98% vs observed +6.46%, a 1.3x gap not an exact match); and the docstring claim that W0 used 'a set this repo did not choose' is false -- the 35-gene list is declared in-file.

power_analysis_headline.w2_gate_vs_detection_floor: loop 153's W2 gate was AUC >= 0.60; the simulated detection floor on that exact set is 0.598 -- zero margin between detectable and declared real
power_analysis_headline.promiscuity_cost: a degron carried by 69% of background must be carried by 84% of oscillators before this experiment can see it
power_analysis_headline.the_decisive_number: at 44% D-box prevalence and a 17.3%-APC positive set, a PERFECTLY penetrant binary degron has a 26% chance of detection; at 69% prevalence, 6%
power_analysis_headline.conclusion: the presence tests were not underpowered by accident, they were arithmetically incapable

diagnoses.loop: LOOP 137 "annotated ubiquitin targeting" (C3) — colab/loop_ubiq_dynamics.py → outputs/loop_ubiq_dynamics.json. Stages U1–U6; final 5/6 with U3 (the test) FAILED.
diagnoses.mechanism: Scheduled ubiquitin-mediated destruction as the explanation for the 362 genes whose PROTEIN is cell-cycle-oscillating (Mahdessian/HPA "CCD Protein" = Yes) while their TRANSCRIPT is not. The loop's own premise (U5, and loop 123's tanh(b*T/4) ceiling) is that a first-order filter dP/dt = k_sp*M − b*P forces protein swing below mRNA swing, so the amplitude can only come from a large, phase-modulated degradation rate constant b — i.e. timed destruction, presumably APC/C- and SCF-driven ubiquitylation.
diagnoses.instrument: A single per-gene STATIC BINARY flag: ub[gene] = ("Glycyl lysine isopeptide" appears in the UniProt Cross-link field) OR ("Ubl conjugation" appears in the Keywords field), OR-reduced across all reviewed human entries sharing a primary gene name (colab/fetch_web.py lines 219-226), serialized as a gene→bool JSON in colab/data/protein_dynamics_source.tsv.gz. 20,190 genes, 3,225 True (15.97% genome-wide). It carries NO E3 identity, NO site count, NO stoichiometry/occupancy, NO rate, NO cell-cycle phase, and NO time dependence — it is "has any curator ever recorded this protein as ubiquitin/Ubl-modified, in any cell type, in any condition". That single bit is what was fed to the Fisher exact in U3 and to every AUC in U4.
diagnoses.effect_size: Primary arm (362 vs 642, the arm the U3 gate reads): 104/359 = 28.97% annotated vs 153/634 = 24.13%, OR = 1.2830, Fisher two-sided p = 9.7628e-02 (log line: "362 vs 642  104/359 against 153/634   OR 1.28   Fisher p = 9.7628e-02"). Secondary arm (362 vs 38): 104/359 vs 12/38 = 31.58%, OR = 0.8671, p = 0.7115 — pointing the WRONG way. Discrimination: annotation → membership-of-the-362 AUC = 0.5270; publication-matched within deciles AUC = 0.5337 (per-decile 0.4676…0.5802). The arithmetic ceiling for a binary score at these rates is 0.5 + (p1−p0)/2 = 0.5242, which the module's own auc() docstring states.
diagnoses.gate_threshold: U3 (the test): gates["U3"] = bool(p_vs_n < 0.05 and orn > 1) — "Fisher exact, two-sided, p < 0.05 with the odds ratio reported. Predeclared expectation: ENRICHED". Observed p = 0.0976, OR = 1.283 → FAIL (direction right, significance not reached). U2 (capability): len(cP) >= 30 and len(cT) >= 30 and ach >= 0.02 → PASS. U4 (fame): bool(not (auc_pub_mem >= auc_ann_mem) and matched > 0.5 + 1e-9) → PASS.
diagnoses.evidence:
1) THE PROPERTY REQUIRED IS A RATE, AND THE LOOP SAYS SO ITSELF. U5 states the requirement as "relative amplitude <= tanh(b*T/4)" with b = ln2/t_half, and prints ceilings 0.9692 / 0.6000 / 0.3333 / 0.1716 / 0.0864 for half-lives 2/6/12/24/48 h. But U5 measures b for ZERO of the 362 — it tabulates five hypothetical half-lives and sets gates["U5"] = True unconditionally ("U5 PASS -- stated and computed"). The kinetic quantity was named, argued from, and never instrumented per gene; the binary annotation was substituted for it.

2) THE RATE WAS ONE DICT KEY AWAY IN AN OBJECT THE LOOP ALREADY LOADED. Line 175 does `import cell_assembled as CA; pubs = CA.load().get("pubs", {})`. That same bundle carries `lifetimes` — 13,329 genes with an explicit per-gene `k_deg_per_h`, the exact b in tanh(b*T/4) — plus `schwan` (4,821 genes with prot_hl_h). I checked coverage on the loop's own split: 142 of the 362 and 307 of the 642 carry a measured k_deg_per_h (median 0.01147 vs 0.00887 /h; t_half 60.4 h vs 78.2 h). The loop pulled `pubs` out of that dict and left the kinetics untouched.

3) THE STATIC PROXY IS NEAR-INFORMATIONLESS AND THE TEST WAS NOT MAINLY UNDERPOWERED. At p0 = 0.2413 with n1 = 359 / n0 = 634, an OR of 1.5 would have landed at z = 2.73 (p ≈ 0.006) and OR 2.0 at z = 4.78. The observed z is 1.65. So the design could have caught a moderate real enrichment; it saw a 4.8-percentage-point drift. The 362-vs-38 arm IS hopeless (n = 38, 12 annotated) and returns OR 0.867, p = 0.7115.

4) PROMISCUITY (secondary). 24.13% of the "neither" background carries the flag; pooled prevalence over the tested 1,031 genes is 269/1031 = 26.09%, versus 15.97% genome-wide — the HPA CCD-called population is a well-studied slice, so the feature is even more common there. A bit carried by a quarter of the background caps binary AUC at 0.5242 even at the observed separation.

5) DILUTION (secondary). "Ever ubiquitylated" is the pan-proteome turnover route; the mechanistic subset that matters — APC/C-Cdh1/Cdc20 and SCF substrates destroyed on a phase schedule — is a minority of the 362 and is pooled with ~255 flag-negative and ~100 flag-positive-but-constitutive genes.

6) NULL CAPABILITY WAS REALLY CHECKED. GG.achievable_change(pooled) = 0.3856736042056106, compared against the U2 bar of 0.02 → PASS. At pooled prevalence 0.2609 the binary bound 2p(1−p) = 0.3857 reproduces exactly, i.e. near the 0.5 binary maximum: the feature vector genuinely varies and the comparison was not vacuous. Note gate_guard.null_can_move was NOT called and no permutation null was run (the seeded rng at line 146 is never used) — the discriminating test is analytic Fisher, so achievable_change is the appropriate and sufficient guard here.

7) FAME WAS CHECKED AND DID NOT FIRE. U4 on n = 892 genes with publication counts (16,492 available): pubs → annotation AUC 0.7169; pubs → membership AUC 0.4760; annotation → membership AUC 0.5270. fame_wins = (0.4760 >= 0.5270) = False; matched-within-decile AUC 0.5337 > 0.5 → U4 PASS. NOTHING WAS STRUCK. Publication count is essentially orthogonal to membership of the 362 (0.476, i.e. slightly below chance), so unlike loops 121 (KEN-box rho +0.2429) and 122 (5'TOP rho +0.3296) the fame confound did not manufacture or destroy this result. It does show the annotation is ~72% predictable from study effort, which attenuates rather than inflates — curation noise on the instrument, not a false positive.

8) COVERAGE. manifest.coverage = {available: 1130, used: 1031, selection: "all", fraction: 0.9123893805309734} (91.2%). Group coverage: 359/362, 38/38, 634/642. U1 reproduced 88/362/38/642 exactly, so the population is right — this is not a wrong-population failure. Minor provenance note, not the failure mode: the manifest records the HPA input from a scratchpad path (/tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/proteinatlas.tsv), not from the repo tree.
diagnoses.fair_test_would_need: Instrument the RATE, not the annotation. (a) Per-gene degradation rate constant b: the loop's own bundle already exposes lifetimes[gene]["k_deg_per_h"] for 13,329 genes (142/362 and 307/642 covered) — test whether b, or the per-gene ceiling tanh(b*T/4) evaluated against each gene's MEASURED Ly et al. amplitude, separates the 362 from the 642, replacing U5's five-row hypothetical table with a per-gene comparison. (b) Phase-resolved occupancy: diGly-remnant ubiquitylome on the same six elutriated NB4 fractions, scored as the CHANGE in site occupancy across the cycle (an amplitude, not a presence bit) — that is the quantity "scheduled destruction" actually predicts. (c) Substrate identity with timing: curated APC/C-Cdc20/Cdh1 and SCF-βTrCP/Skp2/Fbxw7 substrate sets with degradation-assay support, tested as a graded score, so the positive feature is rare enough to separate instead of marking a quarter of the background. (d) Fix the power and the controls: drop the n = 38 arm as a discriminator or pool it, add a matched-abundance control (MS oscillation calling is abundance-dependent and abundance was never controlled here), and keep U4's publication-matched stratification. (e) Keep the achievable_change guard and add an explicit permutation of the group labels with gate_guard.null_can_move on whatever continuous score replaces the bit.

diagnoses.mechanism: Regulated destruction: in dP/dt = k_sp*M - b*P with M flat, protein oscillation must come from b(t) oscillating — timed ubiquitination by APC/C (CDC20/CDH1) and SCF, whose recognition elements are the D-box (R..L, extended R..L..[LIVM]) and KEN-box degrons. The loop tests whether those degron sequences mark the proteins that oscillate. The competing half of the space, k_sp(t) regulated translation, is declared untestable here (5' UTR absent from the repo).
diagnoses.instrument: Per gene: motif hits per 100 residues. densities(s) = 100.0 * len(pattern.findall(s)) / max(len(s),1), where s is the longest UniProt sequence carrying that GN= gene name from human_proteome.fasta.gz (20,213 sequences). Five regexes: D-box "R..L", D-box+ "R..L..[LIVM]", KEN-box "KEN", CDK "[ST]P", CDK "[ST]P.[KR]"; the three degrons feed the gates. This scalar density is fed to the discriminating test S3 as a difference of group means (protein-only mean minus transcript-only mean) with a 2000-round two-sided permutation p on the pooled labels. Non-overlapping regex matching, no disorder/accessibility/surface filter, no phase, no ligase-activity term.
diagnoses.effect_size: S3, the declared discriminating test, came out BACKWARDS on all three degrons. Verbatim from the log: "protein-only minus transcript-only: -0.0314, permutation p = 0.6420" (D-box R..L); "-0.0335, permutation p = 0.2140" (D-box+ R..L..[LIVM]); "-0.0190, permutation p = 0.3080" (KEN-box). Group means (per 100 aa): D-box both 0.5917 > transcript only 0.5868 > neither 0.5653 > protein only 0.5553; KEN both 0.0886 > transcript only 0.0495 > protein only 0.0305 > neither 0.0210. S5 discrimination of CCD vs non-CCD: best sequence feature "SEQ D-box+ R..L..[LIVM] AUC 0.5350", D-box 0.5296, KEN 0.5220. S2 composition-shuffle z: D-box +1.70, D-box+ +1.48, KEN +2.58. Verdict 3/6 with S1, S2, S3 all FAIL.
diagnoses.gate_threshold: S3 (discriminating): "Gate: higher AND a permutation p < 0.05 on the difference" — code `if not (obs > 0 and p < S3_P)`, S3_P = 0.05. Observed obs < 0 for all three degrons, so it failed on SIGN, not on p. S2: "Gate: real above both [nulls] at z >= 2", S2_Z = 2.0. S1: "|Spearman(feature, publication count)| < 0.15 for every motif density", S1_RHO = 0.15. S5: "the best SEQUENCE feature must beat publication count" (|AUC-0.5|). S6: S6_TOL = 1e-9 on the beta=0 reduction, AMP_MIN = 0.20.
diagnoses.evidence:
DECISIVE: the instrument is NOT dead — it is pointed at the wrong set. Recomputing from the same FASTA + proteinatlas.tsv, KEN-box density gives AUC 0.6899 for "both"-oscillate (n=87) vs "neither" (n=634), and 49.4% of the "both" group carries >=1 KEN against 12.3% of "neither" (4.0x). The same instrument on the loop's chosen positive set reads AUC 0.5122 (protein-only vs neither) and 0.4025 — backwards — for protein-only vs transcript-only, with only 14.8% of protein-only genes carrying >=1 KEN, i.e. indistinguishable from the 12.3% background. D-box+ likewise: AUC 0.6011 both-vs-neither, 0.4968 protein-only-vs-transcript-only. A feature that separates at 0.69 on the population the mechanism belongs to and 0.40 on the population the loop tested is a population error, not an instrument error. The loop's own after-the-fact section says exactly this: "The degron signal sits in BOTH-oscillate, the group that already has a transcriptional source... The 359 protein-only oscillators... carry the LEAST of it."

OUTER POPULATION ERROR: the repo's target is ~77-209 proteins oscillating in Ly et al. 2014 mass-spec (elutriated NB4, 6 fractions). Loop 121 never touches it. grep of loop_degron.py returns no Ly/NB4/mass-spec reference, and the manifest inputs are human_proteome.fasta.gz, proteinatlas.tsv, cell_complete.json, _schwan2011.json — no Ly file (other loops, e.g. colab/loop_ms_cellcycle.py and colab/loop_pulse_identify.py, do use it). The substituted positive set is HPA "CCD Protein" immunofluorescence calls, 727 Yes / 765 No — a different assay (IF intensity per cell) in different cells. The loop's own post-hoc proves that substituted label is substantially an imaging property, not an abundance property: dual-compartment annotation gives AUC 0.5992, beating EVERY sequence feature (best 0.5350), CCD 88.9% multi-compartment vs non-CCD 69.0%, difference +19.8%, permutation p = 0.0000, and it survives IF-reliability stratification at AUC 0.5953.

PROMISCUITY (secondary, real): recomputed base rates — D-box R..L is present in 86.0% of the non-CCD controls and 81.1% of the whole proteome, mean 3.38 hits per non-CCD protein vs 4.18 per CCD protein; D-box+ 44.3% of controls; CDK [ST]P 90.7%. The docstring concedes "R..L occurs 3.4 times in an average protein by chance." Consequently D-box AUC 0.5296 and the composition-preserving shuffle cannot be cleared: z +1.70 (D-box) and +1.48 (D-box+), i.e. the CCD/non-CCD gap is inside what scrambling each protein's own residues produces. Only the rare motif, KEN (11.0% proteome-wide), clears both nulls (label z +2.55, composition z +2.58).

DILUTION (secondary): the KEN enrichment is genuine but confined to 87 of the 727 CCD calls (12%), so it is swamped inside S2/S5 — KEN AUC over the full 727 vs 765 is only 0.5220 despite the 49.4%-vs-12.3% separation inside the "both" subgroup.

STATIC-FOR-KINETIC (secondary): the target quantity is b(t), a time-varying rate; the instrument is a phase-less regex count with no accessibility/disorder filter, no ligase-activity term, no phospho-dependency for SCF degrons. The docstring admits it: "a motif has no phase -- the timing lives in the ligase's own activity, which is not in this repository."

POWER (secondary, not binding): the negative arm is 38 genes. But all three point estimates are negative, so the gate `obs > 0 and p < 0.05` failed on direction; more n would sharpen the backwards result, not rescue it.

NULL CAPABILITY: checked, via gate_guard.null_can_move. Label shuffle: changed 0.5027 against achievable 0.4997, threshold 0.2498, "capable": true, for all three degrons. Composition shuffle: "changes 92.1% of residue positions (achievable 93.1%) -- capable". Nulls had real spread (label null_sd 0.0219 / 0.0095 / 0.0047; sequence null_sd 0.0175 / 0.0108 / 0.0033). The S3 permutation null is not explicitly capability-checked but is plainly not inert (p spread 0.214-0.642). Not an inert-null failure.

FAME: two controls ran, nothing was struck. S1 (|rho| < 0.15 vs publication count over 16,492 genes) FAILED — KEN-box rho +0.2429 and CDK [ST]P.[KR] rho +0.2196 exceed the gate; D-box -0.0103, D-box+ +0.0446, [ST]P +0.0175 pass; protein length vs pubs rho +0.1815. Note the defect: the most fame-correlated degron (KEN, rho 0.243) is the ONLY one that survives both S2 nulls, it was NOT struck, and it was carried into S2/S3/S5; the S1 log line also prints the unconditional text "every motif density is under |rho| 0.15" beside the word FAIL. Fame nonetheless cannot explain this loop's failure: publication count AUC is 0.4881 (|AUC-0.5| = 0.0119, pointing the wrong way), phosphosite 0.5059, GO ubiquitin/proteasome 0.4925 — the loop's own reading is correct that "fame lost by being USELESS, not by the biology being strong."

COVERAGE: 1492 used / 1524 available = 0.979 (97.9%), selection "filtered", seed 12100, 4 inputs, 6 controls, 0 warnings, 12.7 s runtime.

WHAT THE PASSES ARE WORTH: S4 (p = 0.001) and S6 (p = 0.0100) are the same quantity, gain(bbar,T), read as a threshold and as an amplitude — the loop says so itself ("S6 is S4 restated through the integrator"). S4 also reports 62.6% of measured CCD proteins sit ABOVE the 24.5 h half-life threshold, where timed destruction cannot produce a 20% swing at all.
diagnoses.fair_test_would_need: (1) The right positive set. Test the actual target — the 77-209 Ly et al. 2014 mass-spec oscillators from elutriated NB4 — against MS-quantified non-oscillators from the same 6 fractions, so the label measures abundance rather than IF intensity per cell. As run, the loop's label is contaminated by relocalisation/imaging (dual-compartment AUC 0.5992 beats every sequence feature). (2) Stop conditioning on "protein-only". Degrons demonstrably live in the periodically-transcribed-AND-destroyed group; the honest comparison is APC/C-substrate-like ("both", n=87, KEN AUC 0.6899) vs background, with protein-only reserved for the k_sp(t) hypothesis. (3) A degron instrument that is not a chance count: restrict matches to IUPred/AlphaFold-disordered, surface-exposed, terminally-accessible regions, weight by position and by known CDC20/CDH1 consensus (RxxLxxxxN, full KEN context), and validate against a curated APC/C-substrate list — a bare R..L is carried by 86% of the background and its group difference does not clear a composition shuffle (z 1.70). (4) Measure the rate, not the motif: per-protein cell-cycle-resolved degradation rates (pulse-SILAC / Bachman-Schwanhausser style k_deg across fractions, or ubiquitylome time-course) to get b(t) with a phase, since the mechanism is kinetic and a static motif has none. (5) Strike, do not merely report, features failing the declared S1 fame prerequisite — KEN-box (rho +0.2429) was the load-bearing motif and should have been excluded or orthogonalised against publication count before S2/S3. (6) Power the negative arm: 38 transcript-only genes cannot support a difference-of-means permutation test; pool across cell lines or use a matched background of several hundred.

diagnoses.loop: LOOP 118 "relocalisation / spatial proteome" — colab/loop_spatial_proteome.py -> outputs/loop_spatial_proteome.json. Six predeclared gates (Q1-Q6) built on Itzhak et al. 2016 eLife 16950 "Dynamic Organellar Maps", sheet "Compact HeLa Spatial Proteome", 8,710 HeLa proteins. ALL SIX GATES PASSED (gates dict in JSON is all-true). The loop did not fail on its own terms; it failed the repo's actual question because that question is never posed in it.
diagnoses.mechanism: Proposed: proteins that appear to oscillate in whole-cell abundance are actually RELOCALISING between compartments through the cycle, so a measurement that captures WHERE a protein is and HOW MUCH of it there is "in the same act" should identify the pulsed set. As implemented, the loop instead used Itzhak's spatial proteome to repair three unrelated infrastructure defects inherited from loops 92/102/116 — a broken PaxDb abundance distribution, all-or-nothing compartment assignment, and a 38.5 mg/mL cytosolic crowding number. Note also the untested physical premise: relocalisation is mass-conserving, so it cannot by itself change whole-cell abundance in Ly's lysate MS unless localisation gates degradation — that coupling is never stated or tested.
diagnoses.instrument: Per gene, four raw columns lifted from the Itzhak sheet (lines 128-131): "Estimated Copy number per cell", "Mol. weight [kDa]", "Cytosolic Pool" fraction (fillna(0).clip(0,1); median 0.196, quartiles 0.001/0.810), and "Compartment Prediction" (14-category static label). Three derived per-gene quantities were fed to gates: (1) Q2 — copy-number rank, Spearman'd against Schwanhausser prot_copies; (2) Q3 — a per-(reaction,gene) BOOLEAN, "does ITZ_TO_GEM[measured compartment] appear among {x.compartment for x in reaction.metabolites}", i.e. does the measured address match the compartment of the gene's own Human-GEM reaction; (3) Q4/Q6 — mass contribution cn*cytf*MW*1000*DA_TO_G, summed over all genes into ONE scalar (163.3 mg/mL). NO per-gene quantity was ever contrasted between pulsed and non-pulsed proteins. There is no discriminating test on the oscillation question in this file.
diagnoses.effect_size: On the oscillation question: NONE — no effect size was computed, because no pulsed/non-pulsed contrast exists. Verbatim from the log, the effect sizes that WERE computed: Q1 "max/median 1,434", "top 1% hold 33.8%, top 10% hold 79.5%", median 82,633 / mean 899,834, total 7.84e+09 molecules/cell. Q2 "Spearman +0.7253" over "4,144 shared genes", "median copy-number ratio Itzhak/Schwanhausser 5.52x". Q3 (the only discriminating comparison in the file, and it is about annotation quality, not pulsing) "ANNOTATION (`comp` label) agrees with its own reaction's compartment: 9,356/23,225 = 40.3%" vs "MEASUREMENT (Itzhak) agrees: 3,187/5,917 = 53.9%" — a +13.6 point gap on UNMATCHED denominators. Q4 "cytosol at 52% of a 3,000 um^3 cell -> 163.3 mg/mL", "whole-cell average protein concentration -> 178.0 mg/mL". Q5 "Large Protein Complex 66.0% -> 28.8% delta -37.3%", "Cytosol (recovered) 0.0% -> 47.7%". Q6 "real +163.3211 null +126.6057 +/- 5.3194 z +6.9 survives 78%", "pubs vs measured copy number: rho +0.4398 over 7,202 genes".
diagnoses.gate_threshold: Q1: "mean must exceed median, max/median must exceed 100, and the top decile must hold more than half the mass" (Q1_MAXMED=100.0, Q1_TOP10=0.50) — observed 1,434 and 79.5%, PASS. Q2: "Spearman >= 0.5" (Q2_RHO=0.50) — observed +0.7253, PASS. Q3: "measurement must beat annotation", coded `q3 = bool(mes_ok/mes_n > ann_ok/ann_n)` — 53.9% > 40.3%, PASS. Q4: "gate: cytosol inside 100-400 mg/mL" (Q4_LO=100.0, Q4_HI=400.0) — observed 163.3, PASS. Q5: hardcoded `"Q5 dual localisation quantified": True` — no gate at all, a reporting step passed by literal. Q6: `q6 = bool(cap["capable"])` — the null-capability boolean ONLY; the fame rho and the survival z are printed but enter no gate. NO gate anywhere references pulsed proteins, cell-cycle amplitude, or Ly et al.

(1) ZERO CONTACT WITH THE PHENOTYPE. `grep -niE "pulse|oscill|cell.?cycle|NB4|elutriat|Ly et al|G1/S|G2/M|phase"` over all 321 lines of colab/loop_spatial_proteome.py returns nothing. (a) POPULATION: load the Ly et al. 2014 NB4 six-fraction table, define positives by a predeclared amplitude statistic (the repo's loop 143 "A" with its BH q<0.05, or the withdrawn 294-gene list used explicitly as a labelled set), and define negatives as the expressed, quantified-in-all-six-fractions background — then score the spatial feature ONLY on genes present in both datasets, reporting that intersection as the real n. (b) INSTRUMENT WITH A TIME AXIS: the "Compact HeLa Spatial Proteome" sheet is one asynchronous snapshot, so the testable quantity must become delta(cytosolic pool fraction) or delta(compartment) BETWEEN cell-cycle states — Itzhak's own dynamic maps (the EGF/translocation arm of the same paper) or a published cell-cycle-resolved organellar map, ideally in a suspension/leukaemic line rather than HeLa. diagnoses.loop: 145 — "phosphodegrons, naive" (colab/loop_phosphodegron.py → outputs/loop_phosphodegron.json). Premise: loops 1-8 all tested constant properties; loop 121 searched only APC/C degrons (D-box, KEN-box) which APC/C binds without phosphorylation. Loop 145 searches the phospho-DEPENDENT SCF degrons instead — beta-TrCP `DSG..S` and Fbw7 CPD `[LIVMP].[ST]P..[ST]` — arguing "the motif is present in the genome from birth; the PHOSPHATE is what arrives on schedule."
diagnoses.mechanism: SCF-family (beta-TrCP / Fbw7) phosphodegron-driven timed ubiquitination: a protein carries a degron whose F-box receptor binds only after a kinase phosphorylates the serine/threonine inside it, so the destruction is timed by the phosphorylation, not by the sequence. If this is what pulses the cell-cycle proteins, the pulsed set should be enriched for degrons whose S/T is actually phosphorylated.
diagnoses.instrument: Per gene, a binary co-location flag. For each motif M the sequence is regex-scanned (`hits` returns 1-based [start,end] spans); UniProt curated `MOD_RES <n>; /note="Phospho...` positions are parsed from colab/data/uniprot_human_ptm.tsv.gz into a per-gene set `st`; then `occ_M = int(any(any(a <= q <= b for q in st) for a,b in hits))` — 1 iff at least one ANNOTATED phosphosite position falls inside at least one motif match. The discriminating feature at P5 is `occ_any = occ_betaTrCP OR occ_Fbw7`. P3 additionally scores the raw copy count `n_M`. No time axis, no phase, no stoichiometry: `occ_any` is one number per gene, identical in G1 and G2.

diagnoses.evidence:
PRIMARY — the instrument has no time axis, which is the exact thing the loop's own argument requires. The docstring: "The only property of a protein that varies on the timescale of a cell cycle is its MODIFICATION STATE" and "The motif is present in the genome from birth; the PHOSPHATE is what arrives on schedule." What was computed is `occ = int(any(a <= q <= b))` over UniProt curated MOD_RES positions — an assertion that a site EXISTS somewhere in the literature, not that it is occupied at a phase. The repo already wrote this rule down and loop 145 broke it: colab/ptm_sites.py:12-18 states "A UniProt MOD_RES line says A SITE EXISTS -- somewhere, in some tissue, in some experiment ... and 27% of the time inferred from a mouse ortholog rather than observed in human at all. It does NOT say the site is occupied," and ptm_sites.py:750 stores `occupancy_measured: False` with the note that the flag exists "so a downstream model cannot quietly promote a site's existence into a site's activity." Loop 145 promoted site existence into scheduled site activity. `occ_any` is a static binary, as time-invariant as loop 121's `R..L` count — the loop swapped one constant property for another constant property one annotation deeper and did not test the key being turned.

The instrument is also crude even as a static motif search: 7 of 11 textbook substrates have ZERO copies of their own ligase's motif — "CDC25A betaTrCP motif copies 0", "CDC25B ... 0", "WEE1 ... 0" (all three carry well-documented non-canonical beta-TrCP phosphodegrons), plus JUN 0, MCL1 0. P2 "PASS" at 4/11 (36.4%) is 36% sensitivity on the set the motifs were DEFINED on, and its 5.2% background is `np.mean` of two very unequal per-motif rates (beta-TrCP 48/8020 = 0.60%, Fbw7 781/8020 = 9.74%), which flatters the Fbw7 arm (2/5 = 40% against its true 9.7% background, not 5.2%).

NULL CAPABILITY — `gate_guard` is never imported (grep for gate_guard/null_can_move/achievable_change in the file returns nothing) and there is NO permutation null at all: line 175 creates `rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)` and `rng` is never referenced again. The loop's control is the APC/C falsification arm, and the loop's own hand-rolled capability gate P1 proved half of it INERT: "KEN-box motif in 1,239 phospho-genes; a site lands inside it in 0 (0.0%)", frac_occupied 0.0000, "P1 FAIL -- co-location IS DEGENERATE and can measure nothing". K, E and N cannot carry a phosphate; D-box `R..L` cannot either (2 wildcards only), giving 6.9%. Yet P3 still averaged that arm into `apc_gain` and PASSED on it: KEN's "gain" of -0.0619 is purely the AUC of a constant predictor collapsing to exactly 0.5000, and D-box contributes -0.0654 from the same mechanical effect. So `ph_gain (+0.0094) > apc_gain (-0.0636)` is a comparison against an arm that could not take the treatment — a gate_guard family-two failure, correctly diagnosed in the docstring and then used anyway.

FAME — P4 ran and nothing was struck: "publication count vs NUMBER OF ANNOTATED SITES: rho +0.2908"; occupancy-given-motif rho +0.1804 (beta-TrCP, n=206) and +0.1718 (Fbw7, n=1,980) against a `worst < 0.25` bar (loops 121/122 were struck at +0.2429 and +0.3296). It passed, but only just, and the bigger fame exposure is unpoliced: the entire pool is the phospho-ANNOTATED 8,020 genes, a fame-selected 39.7% of the proteome.

WRONG POPULATION — P5 tests the HPA immunofluorescence 88/362/38/642 split, not the Ly et al. 2014 MS oscillators the arc is trying to explain. The repo's own loop 123 (outputs/loop_ms_cellcycle.json v4) records n_confirmed 42 against n_denied 273 — only 42 of 315 quantified HPA CCD calls are confirmed by the mass spectrometer. The Ly file (`LY = LR.SC / "ly2014_supp1-v1.txt"`) is present in the repo and used by loop_ms_cellcycle and loop_pulse_identify; loop 145 did not use it. Worse, P3's positives are 11 textbook SCF substrates, not oscillators at all — "scored on 8,020 phospho-annotated genes, 11 of them textbook SCF substrates" (11 positive / 8,009 negative), so the loop's declared centrepiece never touches the phenomenon.

PROMISCUITY / DILUTION — the Fbw7 CPD hits 2,208/8,020 = 27.5% of the pool and D-box hits 7,053/8,020 = 88.0%; `occ_any` is carried by 14.6% of the "neither" background, so the feature is common enough that a real minority signal cannot lift the group rate. And beta-TrCP + Fbw7 are 2 of ~70 human F-box receptors, so any pulsed protein destroyed by a different SCF, by APC/C, or by a non-degron route is scored 0.

COVERAGE — manifest: available 20,213, used 8,020, selection "all", fraction 0.3968 (39.7%); log line "manifest: 3 inputs, coverage 8020/20213 (39.7%) by 'all', seed 14500, controls 5". The phospho-annotation filter also drops 39% of the target split itself: P5's four groups total 83+225+29+356 = 693 of the 1,130 genes in the 88/362/38/642 split, and the genes it drops are the un-annotated, i.e. the un-famous.

WHAT P5 ACTUALLY SHOWS — not merely null but backwards, and the same direction loop 121 got: "protein only" (the group whose protein oscillates while its transcript does not, i.e. exactly the post-transcriptional-destruction group) has the LOWEST occupancy of all four at 10.7%, below "neither" at 14.6% and well below "both" at 22.9% (n=83). At 225 vs 356 this is not a power-limited null — a 2x enrichment (14.6% → 29%) would have been comfortably detected; the observed direction is negative.
diagnoses.fair_test_would_need: A time-resolved phospho-occupancy measurement on the same axis as the abundance data, not a curated annotation. Concretely: (a) a cell-cycle phosphoproteome (e.g. Olsen 2010 mitotic, or an elutriated NB4 phospho run matching Ly et al.) giving, per gene per fraction, the log2 intensity of the specific phosphopeptide covering the degron S/T, so the instrument becomes a per-gene TRAJECTORY of degron-site occupancy rather than a 0/1 existence flag — then test whether the rise of degron-site occupancy precedes the fall of protein abundance in the SAME protein, which is the causal shape the hypothesis actually predicts and which is self-controlled against fame and abundance; (b) the positive set must be the Ly et al. MS oscillators (77-209) already in the repo at ly2014_supp1-v1.txt, or at minimum the 42 MS-confirmed HPA calls, not the 362 imaging calls of which 273/315 are MS-disconfirmed; (c) a degron search with the sensitivity to find CDC25A, CDC25B, WEE1, JUN and MCL1 — a PSSM or ELM-instance-based scan scored against a length- and composition-matched shuffle, since the exact regex returns 0 copies for 7 of 11 textbook substrates; (d) coverage of the SCF family beyond two receptors, or an explicit statement that the test only addresses beta-TrCP and Fbw7 substrates; (e) a falsification arm that can chemically take the treatment (a phospho-independent degron containing an S or T), plus `gate_guard.null_can_move`/`achievable_change` on the label vector and a real permutation null — the KEN arm's occupancy of 0/1,239 makes its -0.0619 an arithmetic artefact, and the P3 PASS rests on it.

diagnoses.loop: LOOP 153 "D-box quality (lysine proximity)" — colab/loop_dbox_quality.py -> outputs/loop_dbox_quality.json. Gates: W0 PASS, W1 FAIL, W2 FAIL (the discriminating test), W3 PASS, W4/W5/W6 PASS (5/7).
diagnoses.mechanism: APC/C-mediated cell-cycle proteolysis, tested not as degron PRESENCE (already killed in loops 121/145/146) but as degron QUALITY. Following Lu, Wang & Kirschner (Science 2015;348:1248737, PMID 25859049) "processive affinity amplification": the APC binds the D-box weakly and transiently, and ubiquitination only initiates if a lysine is close enough to be charged during that contact, after which conjugated ubiquitin raises substrate affinity 40-60-fold. Lysine density near the D-box is therefore the sequence-computable correlate of whether the first round of ubiquitin transfer can happen at all. Prediction: pulsed proteins should carry higher-quality (lysine-rich) D-boxes than MS-flat proteins.
diagnoses.instrument: Per gene: `k_best` = max over all matches of the ELM DEG_APCC_DBOX_1 regex `.R..L..[LIVM].` (overlapping, via lookahead `(?=(...))`) in the UniProt human FASTA sequence, of the count of literal "K" characters in the window seq[max(0,p-60) : min(len,p+60)] around each match start p (dbox_features(), lines 199-213; WINDOW=60, taken from Lu 2015, not fitted). Genes with zero regex hits return None and are dropped entirely. The resulting scalar k_best per gene is fed to auc(oscillators, flat) where the label is Ly-2014 peak-fold >= 2.0 across three pooled fraction-pairs (F1F2/F3F4/F5F6). Secondary instruments in W4: n_dbox, first_pos_frac, n_full_consensus (R..L....N), k_mean.
diagnoses.effect_size: W2 (the discriminating test): AUC_raw = 0.5381324141445599; AUC_length_residualised = 0.5325107584722969; mean lysines-within-60 oscillators 8.4038 vs flat 7.8936, enrichment +6.46% ("lysines within 60 residues: oscillators 8.40, flat 7.89   enrichment +6.5%"); abundance-matched null mean AUC 0.4852, p = 0.0239880059970015. W4 components all near-null: k_mean AUC 0.5439, full-consensus AUC 0.5257, D-box count AUC 0.5188, N-terminal position AUC 0.4485. By contrast W0 (external reproduction on Lu's own comparison) gave substrates 10.04 vs random D-box proteins 6.66, ENRICHMENT +50.6% (0.5064665821715251), p = 0.0005 — so the same instrument DOES work on the right population.
diagnoses.gate_threshold: W2: "Gate: AUC >= 0.60 with p < 0.01 against an abundance-matched null" (W2_AUC_MIN=0.60, W2_P_MAX=0.01), conjoined in code with the fame control and the residualised score: `ok2 = bool(a_raw >= W2_AUC_MIN and p2 < W2_P_MAX and ok3a and a_res >= W2_AUC_MIN)`. Observed 0.538 / p 0.024 — failed on AUC by 0.062 and on p by 2.4x. Supporting gates: W0 "within a factor of two of the published +64%" (W0_FACTOR=2.0, i.e. 0.32-1.28) plus p<0.05 — PASSED at +50.6%; W1(a) proteome D-box fraction in [0.50, 0.85] — FAILED at 0.4405; W1(b) presence AUC in [0.45, 0.55] — passed at 0.5323; W3 fame |rho| < 0.20 (W3_RHO_MAX) — passed at +0.1209.
diagnoses.evidence:
1) THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT BROKEN — W0 proves it transfers. On 25 of 35 declared published APC substrates the identical k_best score gives 10.04 vs 6.66 lysines, +50.6% against 2000 resamples, p=0.0005, within a factor of two of Lu's published +64%. Any failure mode claiming the quantity is meaningless has to explain this.

2) THE POSITIVE SET IS ~83% NON-APC. The file's own addendum: "the 209 oscillators contain only 24 known APC substrates. Among D-box carriers it is 18 of 104 = 17.3%." Dilution arithmetic recorded in the JSON: w0_enrichment 0.506 x apc_fraction 0.173 = predicted_enrichment 0.088 vs observed_enrichment 0.065. The observed +6.5% is what a 17.3%-pure positive set predicts from a +50.6% pure effect.

3) THE GATE WAS ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE. My own back-calculation from the reported numbers: if the 82.7% non-APC oscillators sit at AUC 0.50 against flat, the observed pooled 0.5381 implies the 18 APC substrates separate from flat at AUC = (0.5381 - 0.827*0.5)/0.173 = 0.720 — comfortably past the 0.60 gate. To drag the POOLED AUC to 0.60 at 17.3% purity, the APC subset would need AUC = (0.60 - 0.827*0.5)/0.173 = 1.078. Impossible. The 0.60 gate could not be cleared no matter how real the mechanism is, given this positive set.

4) THE MECHANISM IS PRESENT, NOT ABSENT — the label direction was independently validated. Addendum: "24 of 31 published APC substrates quantified by Ly are called oscillating (77.4%) against a base rate of 209/6372 = 3.3%. A 23.6x enrichment." So APC substrates ARE in the positive set; they just do not dominate it. This rules out wrong-population (the mechanism's population is inside the positives) and rules out genuinely-absent.

5) THE WITHIN-POSITIVE SALVAGE CONFIRMS DILUTION AND WAS THEN STRUCK FOR FAME. "can the lysine score find the 18 known APC substrates among the 104 D-box-carrying oscillators?" result_auc 0.6092 — i.e. the score DOES rank the APC minority above the rest of the positives, clearing 0.60. But verdict "STRUCK": pubs_apc 308 vs pubs_other 130, auc_pubs 0.8049, "The label is 80% recoverable from publication count alone, far past the loop-137 threshold." The file correctly notes the SCORE is clean (rho(pubs,k_best)=+0.1209 < 0.20) and it is the LABEL that is fame — so the confound sits on the salvage test only, not on W2.

6) NULL CAPABILITY WAS NEVER FORMALLY CHECKED. grep of colab/loop_dbox_quality.py shows gate_guard is imported but only `GG.verdict` is called (lines 279, 305, 381). Neither `GG.achievable_change` nor `GG.null_can_move` appears anywhere in the file, and the file is absent from the 30-file grep hit list for those functions. The null was nonetheless demonstrably NOT inert: 2000 decile-abundance-matched resamples produced a spread wide enough that ~2.4% exceeded the real value (p=0.0240) with mean 0.4852, so inert-null is excluded on the evidence even though the guard was skipped. One residual flaw: nullA compares picked flat genes against f_k, the full flat vector that CONTAINS them, which biases the null slightly toward 0.5 — a minor, conservative-direction defect.

7) SECONDARY — PROMISCUITY AND HALF THE POSITIVES DROPPED. W1(a) failed: "fraction of the proteome carrying a D-box: 44.1%" against a 50-85% gate; 48.3% of flat proteins carry the motif against 54.7% of oscillators. The negative set is therefore half-contaminated with the same motif. Worse, the ELM regex `.R..L..[LIVM].` is stricter than bare RxxL (the addendum diagnoses this correctly), so only 104 of 209 oscillators (49.8%) survived to be scored — half the positive set was discarded before the test ran, compounding dilution.

8) COVERAGE IS REPORTED AS 100% AND IT IS TAUTOLOGICAL. Manifest: available 2821, used 2821, selection "filtered", fraction 1.0. But `available=len(shared)` is itself the D-box-carrying subset, so the fraction is 1.0 by construction. Honest coverage: 104/209 = 49.8% of oscillators, 2717/6163 = 44.1% of flat, 2821/6372 = 44.3% of Ly-quantified proteins.

9) POWER IS MARGINAL BUT SECONDARY. Hanley-McNeil SE at n1=104, n2=2717 is ~0.0294, so the observed 0.5381 is +1.30 SE above 0.50 and +1.80 SE above the abundance-matched null mean. More n would have made the +6.5% enrichment significant, but would never have moved the AUC to 0.60 — which is why underpowered is secondary to dilution.

10) THE FILE PREDECLARED ITS OWN LIMIT AND HONOURED IT. W6: "lysine proximity is a SEQUENCE PROXY for a KINETIC quantity... Counting lysines near a regex is not that." True, and it is a real secondary mode — but W0's +50.6% shows the static proxy retains enough of the kinetic signal to separate APC substrates from random D-box proteins, so the proxy gap alone does not account for the collapse from +50.6% to +6.5%. Purity does, exactly, to within 0.088 vs 0.065.
diagnoses.fair_test_would_need: Stop asking a diluted question. Concretely: (a) DEFINE THE POSITIVE SET BY THE MECHANISM'S SIGNATURE, not by MS oscillation per se — restrict to oscillators whose Ly-2014 trajectory shows the mitosis-exit-timed sawtooth (sharp drop between the M-phase and G1 fractions, slow rebuild) rather than any >=2-fold peak-to-trough. That selects the APC-competent subpopulation instead of pooling it with 83% of proteins whose pulsing has some other cause. (b) POWER THE TEST TO THE ACHIEVABLE CEILING, not to a wished-for one: predeclare the gate from the estimated purity of the positive set. At 17.3% purity the maximum pooled AUC is ~0.55, so a 0.60 gate is self-refuting; either raise purity first or gate on the within-positive-set contrast. (c) FIX THE LABEL-FAME PROBLEM THAT STRUCK THE SALVAGE TEST — replace the hand-declared 35-gene literature substrate list (which is fame-selected, auc_pubs 0.8049) with an unbiased ground truth: APC/C-degron proteomics or a CDC20/CDH1-depletion stabilisation screen, or at minimum a publication-count-matched substrate/non-substrate pairing so the 0.6092 within-oscillator result becomes readable. (d) BROADEN MOTIF DETECTION so the positive set is not halved — use bare RxxL plus KEN plus ABBA, which is what Lu's 69% actually refers to (the addendum identifies this: "Lu 2015's 69% is for D AND KEN boxes combined"), instead of ELM's stricter `.R..L..[LIVM].` at 44.1%. (e) CALL gate_guard.null_can_move on the abundance-matched null's input vector, and fix the null so resampled flat genes are compared against the flat pool EXCLUDING themselves. (f) Ideally, replace the static proxy with a measured one — ubiquitination-site occupancy (diGly proteomics) or degradation half-life from a pulse-chase/Ub-fusion assay — since W6's own admission stands: a lysine count is not a rate.
secondary_failure_modes: wrong-property-static-proxy-for-kinetic — W6 declares it: lysine count near a regex is a static stand-in for processivity, a single-molecule rate. Secondary rather than primary because W0's +50.6% (p=0.0005) proves the static proxy DOES carry the signal on the correct population; the proxy gap cannot explain the drop to +6.5% when purity arithmetic explains it exactly (predicted 0.088, observed 0.065).

promiscuous-feature — the D-box is carried by 44.1% of the proteome and 48.3% of the flat negatives, so the negative set is half-loaded with the same motif; this is why presence gave AUC 0.5323 and why the graded score starts from a contaminated baseline. Also cost 50% of the positives (only 104/209 oscillators carried an ELM D-box).

diagnoses.loop: LOOP 146 — "phosphodegrons, ELM curated" (colab/loop_elm_degron.py → outputs/loop_elm_degron.json). diagnoses.mechanism: Phosphodegron-mediated destruction: a cell-cycle kinase phosphorylates a short linear degron (beta-TrCP DSGxxS, Fbw7 CPD, SKP2-CKS1), the phosphate creates the E3 binding epitope, SCF ubiquitinates and the protein is destroyed — so proteins whose degrons are phospho-occupied should be the ones that pulse. The loop's test of this: does knowing a degron motif is phospho-occupied (rather than merely present) add discriminating power, specifically for degrons whose binding REQUIRES the phosphate and not for degrons that merely contain S/T?
diagnoses.instrument: Two per-gene quantities per ELM degron class k, computed over the 8,020 genes that have both a proteome sequence and >=1 UniProt MOD_RES "Phospho" annotation (lines 292-310): present[g] = len(list(re.finditer(ELM_class_regex, seq[g]))), an integer count of regex matches; occupied[g] = int(any annotated phosphosite position q of gene g falls inside any matched window [m.start()+1, m.end()]), a strict binary. The discriminating statistic fed to the gate is the per-class AUC DIFFERENCE gain_k = AUC(occupied, y) - AUC(present, y), where y = "g is one of ELM's curated true-positive substrate genes for class k", averaged over the testable classes in each arm. Q5 uses a derived binary occ_any[g] = OR of occupied[g] over the 4 PHOSPHO-REQUIRED classes. Critically, occupied[g]=1 implies present[g]>=1 — occupancy is a lossy binarization nested strictly inside presence.

diagnoses.evidence:
WHY STATIC-PROXY-FOR-KINETIC DOMINATES. occupied[g] is a single time-invariant bit: "has any deposited study ever mapped a phosphosite inside any window matching this degron regex." It is a union over every cell type, condition and cell-cycle phase in UniProt. The mechanism requires the opposite — the degron must be phosphorylated AT a phase and the cognate E3 active THEN. Two proteins with identical DSGxxS motifs and identical annotated sites differ in pulse behaviour entirely by kinase/E3 timing, which this bit cannot see. The proof that the static bit is the problem, not the statistic: Q5 uses a clean, non-doomed instrument (binary occ_any, Fisher, n=225 vs 356) directly against the oscillator split and returns 10.7% vs 10.4%, p = 1.0000 — dead flat. The loop's own Q6 text concedes exactly this: "the timing is not in any CONSTANT property this project can measure ... What has never been available is the quantity the physics actually points at: a degradation RATE measured through the cycle." Annotation depth confirms the bit is noise-dominated: median annotated phosphosites per pool gene = 3.0, against real phosphoproteomes of tens of sites per protein, so occupancy is decided by whether one of ~3 sampled sites happens to land in one of a few degenerate windows.

WHY THE Q3 GATE COULD NOT PASS (inert-null / gate-that-cannot-pass). occupied is a strict sub-indicator of present (nocc=1 requires hs non-empty, lines 307-309), so binarizing a graded count with AUC 0.910-0.962 can essentially only lose ranking information. Empirically 14/14 classes negative, min -0.4969, max -0.0346. A gain of +0.02 was arithmetically unreachable by any class in the study, yet the +0.02 bar was never tested for reachability. colab/gate_guard.py exists in this repo and documents this exact fault in its own header — "A gate that cannot pass is the same fault as a null that cannot move, and this module had one in it for fourteen loops" — and exposes achievable_change (line 96) and null_can_move (line 109). loop_elm_degron.py imports only run_manifest, loop_replication and cell_assembled; neither guard is called. The "control that can move" is also barely capable: PHOSPHO-CAPABLE occ rates are DEG_COP1_1 1.1%, DEG_Kelch_Keap1_1 0.41%, DEG_CRL4_CDT2_1 0.0125% — that last is 1 gene in 8,020, and 0 of its 4 positives, i.e. AUC 0.625 is a tie-rank artefact. The predeclared Q2 gate said "all three arms must be non-empty, AND the phospho-capable arm must show non-zero occupancy" (lines 48-49); the shipped gate is gates["Q2"] = bool(all(len(v) > 0 ...) and len(arms["PHOSPHO-CAPABLE"]) >= 3) — it counts CLASSES, never occupancy. The one correction loop 146 was built to make over loop 145's chemically-incapable KEN-box arm was declared and then silently dropped, and Q2 "PASSED" on a check that does not test the claim. The arm taxonomy is also mis-assigned: helper can_hold_phos (line 264) is dead code, never called; arms are assigned by literal [STY] characters in the regex (line 275), so wildcard-containing regexes are called INCAPABLE. DEG_APCC_DBOX_1 (".R..L..[LIVM].") sits in PHOSPHO-INCAPABLE with occ rate 2.8% — higher than every class in the CAPABLE arm and higher than DEG_SCF_TRCP1_1 (1.1%) in the REQUIRED arm. The "floor" arm is not a floor.

FAME. Q4 FAILED: PHOSPHO-REQUIRED mean rho +0.2090, max |rho| 0.3614 against the 0.25 bar, and the gradient is perfectly monotone across arms — REQUIRED +0.2090, CAPABLE +0.1080, INCAPABLE +0.0437 — i.e. the more "phospho-dependent" the arm, the more its occupancy signal is publication count. The loop declared "Q4 FAIL -- occupancy IS a fame proxy" and folded that into the NOT JUSTIFIED verdict, but no class was removed and no fame-adjusted re-test was run. The pool itself is the fame-selected subset: scoring is restricted to the 8,020 genes with >=1 annotated phosphosite out of 20,213, coverage fraction 0.3968 — 137 of the 362 protein-only oscillators and 286 of the 642 "neither" were dropped for having no phospho annotation at all.

POPULATION AND POWER. Q3's positives are ELM's curated textbook substrates, not oscillators: only 2 of 4 PHOSPHO-REQUIRED classes were testable (n_pos 5 and 15; DEG_SCF_FBW7_2 with 1 and DEG_SCF_SKP2-CKS1_1 with 2 curated genes were dropped by len(tp_genes[k]) < 3), so the headline -0.0841 is the mean of exactly two numbers. The Q6 build verdict is ok = Q1 and Q2 and Q3 and Q4 (line 428) — Q5, the only question that touches the 362, is excluded from the verdict entirely. Base rates measured directly: union of the 4 REQUIRED motifs is PRESENT in 2,600/8,020 = 32.4% of the pool and OCCUPIED in 613/8,020 = 7.6%; per class DEG_SCF_FBW7_1 present 21.5%/occupied 4.9%, DEG_SCF_TRCP1_1 present 7.2%/occupied 1.1%. A feature carried by a third of the background as presence and by ~10% of BOTH the 225 oscillators and the 356 non-oscillators cannot separate them.

WHAT WORKED. Q1 is a genuine, clean instrument check and it passed: 112/116 = 96.6% of validated instances recovered by their own class regex, 0 accessions missing, DEG_SCF_TRCP1_1 16/16 and DEG_APCC_KENBOX_2 11/11. The regexes are correct; the property they measure is the wrong one.
diagnoses.fair_test_would_need: A time-resolved occupancy measurement rather than a static annotation bit: phosphosite stoichiometry per degron window measured in the same 6 elutriated NB4 fractions (phospho-enriched MS on the Ly et al. fractions, or a matched published cell-cycle phosphoproteome), so occupancy becomes a 6-point trajectory whose AMPLITUDE and PHASE — not its existence — are the feature. Pair that with the other half of the rate: cognate E3/adaptor activity windows (APC/C-Cdc20 vs Cdh1, SCF-beta-TrCP, Fbw7) and a directly measured degradation rate per phase (pulse-SILAC or cycloheximide-chase by phase, or Ky/Kd from a turnover dataset). Statistically: (1) score occupancy as a graded quantity NESTED inside presence — fraction of matched windows occupied, or a logistic model of present + occupied, or AUC restricted to the present-positive subset — never AUC(binary sub-indicator) minus AUC(graded superset), which is structurally negative; (2) run gate_guard.achievable_change on the gain statistic to prove +0.02 is reachable before gating on it, and gate_guard.null_can_move on the PHOSPHO-CAPABLE arm to prove it is not near-inert (CRL4_CDT2_1 at 1/8,020 would have been rejected); (3) fix the arm taxonomy by actually calling can_hold_phos so wildcard-matching classes like DEG_APCC_DBOX_1 stop being labelled INCAPABLE; (4) make the discriminating comparison the 362 protein-only oscillators vs a publication-count- and abundance-matched background, with the oscillator set as POSITIVES from the start rather than as an afterthought excluded from the verdict.

137.argument:
STRONGEST CASE AGAINST, then why it fails.

(1) The attack. 'wrong-property' is the self-flattering answer -- it leaves the mechanism alive. The binding constraint here is arguably PROMISCUITY, which disqualifies the instrument before any property argument: the flag marks 24.13% of the background and 26.09% of the tested set, and for a binary score with midranks AUC = 0.5+(p1-p0)/2 EXACTLY, so the reachable discrimination is 0.5737 at OR 2.0, 0.6235 at OR 3.0, 0.6863 at OR 5.0. The loop's docstring asks whether the annotation 'EXPLAINS the 362'; a bit carried by a quarter of the proteome cannot answer that at ANY odds ratio. On that reading U3 was dead on arrival regardless of static-vs-kinetic, and a phase-resolved measure with the same prevalence would fail identically.

(2) The second attack: the diagnosis's dismissal of UNDERPOWERED is overstated. Its evidence item 3 says the design 'could have caught a moderate real enrichment', which I confirm (MDE OR 1.504 at 80% power). But it omits the corollary: resolving the OR 1.283 that actually exists needs n1 approx 1008, and the HPA CCD-Protein/not-CCD-Transcript class is capped at 362 genes. So p=0.0976 is UNDERDETERMINED, not refuted -- this comparison can never adjudicate the effect it found. The honest phrasing is 'excludes OR >= 1.5, cannot adjudicate OR 1.28, and OR 1.28 would be scientifically useless anyway (AUC 0.524)', not 'NOT mainly underpowered'.

(3) The third attack: the diagnosis's own remedy (a) commits the error it diagnoses. I ran U5's promised computation -- median tanh(b*T/4) with the model's measured b is 0.0687 for the 362, and ZERO of 142 reach a 0.5 ceiling. A steady-state, cycle-averaged k_deg is itself a STATIC proxy for the phase-modulated b that 'scheduled destruction' requires. So 'wrong-property' correctly names the fault but is not a rescue: only remedy (b), phase-resolved diGly occupancy CHANGE, is the actual property, and no such data exists in this repo. The diagnosis's confidence:high understates that its preferred fix cannot close the loop either.

(4) WHY THE ATTACKS FAIL AND I CONCEDE. Promiscuity is not independent of staticness here -- it is CAUSED by it. 'Ever ubiquitylated, any cell type, any condition' is promiscuous precisely because the time and occupancy axes were collapsed; a phase-resolved occupancy-change score is rare by construction. The way to settle root cause is to change ONE thing -- the property -- on the same genes, and the loop's own already-loaded bundle lets you do it. I did: k_deg_per_h separates the 362 from the 642 at AUC 0.5704, p=0.0164, in the predicted direction (t_half 60.4 h vs 78.2 h), on a THIRD of the sample (142 vs 307), and it survives publication-quintile matching (0.5762) while the static bit does not clear its gate at n 359 vs 634. Changing the property moves the statistic; that is direct evidence the property was wrong, not that the mechanism is absent. That same result kills 'genuinely-absent' (a degradation signal IS present, p=0.0164) and kills 'confounded-by-fame-or-abundance' (pubs->membership 0.476, i.e. fame ATTENUATES rather than inflates -- matched 0.5337 > unmatched 0.5270 -- and abundance is null at AUC 0.4706, p=0.369). It also kills 'wrong-population': U1 reproduces 88/362/38/642 exactly.

(5) INERT NULL (trap 1) DOES NOT FIRE. GG.achievable_change WAS called and returned 0.3857 = 2p(1-p) at p=0.2609, near the 0.5 binary maximum, against a U2 bar of 0.02 (a 19x margin, so U2 is a weak but correct guard). GG.null_can_move was NOT called and no permutation null was run -- the seeded rng at line 146 is created and never referenced again (verified: 'rng' appears exactly once in the file) -- but the discriminating statistic is an ANALYTIC Fisher exact with no permuted input to compare, so achievable_change is the appropriate and sufficient guard. The comparison was not vacuous.

(6) SLIPS IN THE DIAGNOSIS, all minor and none load-bearing. It calls 0.5+(p1-p0)/2 'the arithmetic ceiling'; for a binary score with midranks that is an exact IDENTITY, not a ceiling -- which is why the reported auc_ann_mem 0.5270 legitimately exceeds 0.5242 (different subsets: 892 with pubs vs 1031 total) without contradiction. It reads AUC 0.7169 as 'the annotation is ~72% predictable from study effort'; AUC is a rank statistic, not a proportion of explained annotation. Its z figures (1.65, 2.73) are 1.672 and 2.78. Its '142 of the 362' is the non-null k_deg count; 300 of 362 are in `lifetimes` at all.

(7) TRAP 5, GATE VS DOCSTRING -- two real mismatches, neither causing the FAIL. U3's docstring predeclares enrichment 'relative to the 38, and relative to the 642' but gates only on p_vs_n; the 38-arm (OR 0.867, p 0.7115, wrong direction) was computed, printed and excluded from the gate. That is LENIENT -- including it would have failed harder -- so it does not explain the failure, but a disconfirming arm was reported with no consequence. More seriously, U5's docstring promises 'Using the model's own measured b, what fraction of the 362 could oscillate at ALL... Gate: report it'; the code uses no measured b, computes no fraction, prints five hypothetical half-lives and sets gates['U5'] = True unconditionally -- while the bundle carrying b was already loaded at line 175. That is an unearned PASS on the loop's headline physical argument, so the 5/6 score overstates what was established; the promised number is 0.0%-0.7%. Minor provenance note: the manifest hashes the HPA input from a session scratchpad path (/tmp/.../scratchpad/proteinatlas.tsv), not the repo tree, so the hash is not reproducible for a re-runner even though the split reproduces exactly.

VERDICT: the diagnosis survives my best attack, on evidence it did not itself produce. Primary mode stands. I would reorder its secondaries to promiscuous-feature (co-primary, caused by the static choice), then underpowered (stronger than it allows: structurally unresolvable at n1=362), then signal-diluted, and I would append 'abundance was never controlled' to the caveats even though I checked it and it is null.

145.argument:
VERIFICATION FIRST. I recomputed the feature from scratch off the same three inputs and reproduced every headline number exactly: pool 8,020/20,213 (39.7%); betaTrCP 236 carriers / 48 occupied (20.3%); Fbw7 2,208 / 781 (35.4%); D-box 7,053 / 487 (6.9%); KEN 1,239 / 0 (0.0%); P5 groups 83/225/29/356 with 19, 24, 4 and 52 occupied; Fisher 0.20649. gate_guard.py does exist and is imported by 30+ other loops, is NOT imported here; `rng` is created at line 175 and never referenced again; there is no permutation null. loop 123's 42 confirmed / 273 denied is real (outputs/loop_ms_cellcycle.json v4, with v3 ms_confirms_ccd = 0.1333); ly2014_supp1-v1.txt is present and unused. So the diagnosis's factual base is largely sound. Its DIAGNOSIS is not.

THE REFUTATION. The diagnosis's own centrepiece sentence is the one that fails: "WHAT P5 ACTUALLY SHOWS — not merely null but backwards ... At 225 vs 356 this is not a power-limited null." Both halves are wrong, and correcting them relocates the failure.

(1) THE ORDERING IS ANNOTATION DEPTH, NOT BIOLOGY. `occ_any` is a near-monotone function of how many phosphosites UniProt has curated: P(occ_any=1) by n_sites bin runs 2.1% (1 site) → 4.8% → 7.8% → 13.5% → 24.6% → 37.0% → 60.0% (33+). rho(occ_any, n_sites) = +0.227. The four HPA groups differ in exactly that: median n_sites is 8 for "both", 4 for "neither", 3 for "protein only" — precisely the rank order of the raw rates 22.9% / 14.6% / 10.7%. Match on n_sites and it evaporates: Mantel-Haenszel OR for both-vs-neither falls from a crude 1.57 to 1.02, and protein-only-vs-neither from 0.73 to 0.80. An annotation-depth-matched permutation gives both p=0.227 and protein-only p=0.464.

I then built the null the loop never built — per gene, place the SAME number of sites at random among that protein's own S/T/Y residues, which controls n_sites, length, motif copy number and composition simultaneously. Observed/expected co-location: both 2.03, protein only 2.28, transcript only 2.45, neither 2.17. Bootstrapped differences: protein-only minus neither +0.114, 95% CI [-0.73, +1.05], p=0.85; both minus neither -0.132, CI [-0.86, +0.69], p=0.72. All four groups carry identical degron co-location enrichment. The direction even FLIPS — protein-only (2.28) sits nominally ABOVE neither (2.17). The "backwards" result the diagnosis treats as a finding is a curation artifact, and it was p=0.2065 to begin with.

(2) IT IS A POWER-LIMITED NULL, by the repo's own numbers. Minimum detectable count is 48/225 = 21.3% (Fisher p=0.042), a 1.46x lift. Simulated power at the observed base rate: 0.14 at 1.2x, 0.28 at 1.3x, 0.60 at 1.5x, 0.98 at 2.0x. The diagnosis's claim that 2x would have been comfortably detected is correct — but 2x was never achievable. Ceiling: only 13.3% of HPA CCD calls are MS-confirmed (loop 123); the instrument is 36% sensitive on textbook substrates (P2, 4/11); betaTrCP+Fbw7 are 2 of ~70 F-box receptors. Even under the biologically impossible best case where every MS-real oscillator in the group is a betaTrCP/Fbw7 substrate, lift = 0.133 × 0.36 × (1−0.146) ≈ 4.0 pp → 18.6% → power ≈ 0.25. Realistically ≈ 1 pp → power ≈ 0.07.

(3) THE FEATURE IS A KINASE-CONSENSUS PROXY. The +0.0094 "phospho gain" is entirely the Fbw7 arm (+0.0524); betaTrCP's gain is NEGATIVE (−0.0335). The Fbw7 CPD regex [LIVMP].[ST]P..[ST] contains S/T-P, the proline-directed CDK/MAPK consensus and the most heavily annotated site class in UniProt: 97.8% of the 781 Fbw7-co-located genes simply have an annotated S/T-P site somewhere, and 57.3% of the whole pool has one. The motif itself hits 27.5% of proteins, near its chance expectation for a 7-mer of that degeneracy. And the sign structure is diagnostic: the arm with a genuine positive-control signal (betaTrCP, 2/6 vs its own 0.60% background, binomial p=0.00053) LOST AUC when occupancy was required, while the arm with no significant positive control (Fbw7, 2/5 vs its own 9.74%, p=0.078) gained. The one positive number in the loop is anti-correlated with where the real substrate signal lives.

(4) A GATE-SCOPE DEFECT THE DIAGNOSIS MISSED. P4 computes `worst = max(abs(v['rho_pubs_occupancy_given_motif']) for k, v in p4.items() if isinstance(v, dict))`. That `isinstance` check silently excludes p4['rho_pubs_nsites'] = +0.2908, a float — a value ABOVE the 0.25 bar that struck loop 121 (+0.2429) and loop 122 (+0.3296). It is exempted on the docstring's theory that "Fame drives how many sites a protein has annotated. It does not drive whether one of them lands in a six-residue window." The P(occ | n_sites) table refutes that theory outright: more sites mechanically means more chances, 2.1% → 60.0% across the range. The exempted correlation is the operative one. Loop 145 was built specifically to evade the fame objection that killed 121 and 122, asserted immunity, and did not achieve it.

WHY NOT THE PROPOSED MODE. "Static proxy for a kinetic property" predicts an attenuated but unbiased null. What the output contains is a graded, ordered pattern fully reproduced by curator attention and fully abolished by a site-placement null. The loop did not measure a degraded version of degron kinetics; it measured annotation depth. Second, time resolution is not required for the question P5 asks — "are the pulsed proteins enriched for betaTrCP/Fbw7 substrates" is an enrichment question about static substrate-hood; the phosphate schedule matters only to the timing claim, which P5 never tests. So the charge misidentifies which question failed. Third, the loop's own data show the static proxy is NOT information-free about substrate identity (betaTrCP, p=0.00053), so "static therefore wrong" is too strong. Fourth, and per the brief, "wrong-property" is the self-flattering reading: it preserves "the mechanism may still be true, we merely used the wrong clock." The unflattering and better-supported reading is that the loop's single differentiating result was curation, and its own fame gate was scoped so it could not see that.

WHAT I CONCEDE. The docstring/instrument mismatch is real and the diagnosis documents it accurately — `occ` asserts a site EXISTS in the literature, and colab/ptm_sites.py:12-18 and the `occupancy_measured: False` flag at :750 already forbade promoting existence into activity. That belongs in the record as a secondary finding. I also concede the inert-null observation on its facts: KEN's occ vector is constant, its AUC is exactly 0.5000 by construction, its −0.0619 is arithmetic, and P3 averaged it in and PASSED on it — a textbook gate_guard Family Two violation, caught by the loop's own P1 and used anyway.

WHY INERT-NULL STILL DOES NOT DOMINATE (trap 1, checked directly). The inert arm made a gate PASS spuriously; it is not why the loop failed. At the headline gate P5 the statistic was demonstrably live: `occ_any` spans 10.7% to 22.9% across the HPA groups, both-vs-protein-only is Fisher p=0.0090, and the minimum significant value 48/225 sits well inside the feature's range. That comparison was not vacuous — it was underpowered and confounded.

ERRORS IN THE DIAGNOSIS. (a) "7 of 11 textbook substrates have ZERO copies of their own ligase's motif" is false. The log shows five zero-copy genes — CDC25A, CDC25B, WEE1, JUN, MCL1 — while FBXO5 has 1 copy and NOTCH1 has 2. Seven is the count lacking OCCUPANCY, not copies; the diagnosis conflates the two and lists only five examples for its seven. (b) "this is not a power-limited null" is refuted above. (c) Treating the reversal as directional evidence is a cherry-pick at p=0.2065, and it inverts under normalization. (d) It notes the pooled 5.2% background flatters Fbw7 but misses that the same pooling badly under-states betaTrCP (2/6 against 0.60%), which is what exposes the sign inconsistency in P3.

BEST ALTERNATIVE TO MY OWN VERDICT. "underpowered"/"signal-diluted" is the serious runner-up — the power ceiling calculation stands on its own and would have sunk this test even with a perfect instrument. I rank it second because a pure power failure produces noise, whereas this output contains a reproducible ordered pattern, and that pattern is the thing the diagnosis reads as biology. Cytosolic pool fraction: pulsed median 0.274 vs background 0.198, AUC 0.5378 (p=0.006). Abundance-decile-matched (200 resamples): AUC 0.5214 +/- 0.0141. That is no discrimination. And the compartment 'signal' that survives unmatched is a detection artifact of abundance: pulsed proteins carry 2.3x the copy number (median 187,513 vs 82,388, AUC 0.613, p=3e-16), so 'no prediction' falls from 39.4% to 22.6% (OR 0.45) and 'Large Protein Complex' rises from 29.8% to 43.8% (OR 1.84) mechanically. So the static spatial feature is not merely unmeasured here -- when measured properly it is null, and its apparent effect is the abundance confound the loop computed (pubs_rho +0.4398) and then dropped from every gate.

4. PROMISCUITY COMPOUNDS IT. The features on offer are carried by half the background: cytosolic pool > 0.20 in 49.7% of 8,710 proteins, 'Large Protein Complex' in 30.0%, and 39.6% have no compartment call at all. Only 1,636/8,710 = 18.8% carry a GEM-mappable organellar label. The docstring's '8,710 proteins, all major organelles, accuracy above 92%' oversells the usable content roughly fivefold.

5. NULL: NOT INERT, BUT THE GATE IS -- AND THE DIAGNOSIS MISSED THAT. The null actually fed to GG.survival permutes cytf (continuous, 8,710 entries) and moves the statistic hard: real 163.32 vs null 126.61 +/- 5.32, z +6.9. Not vacuous. The diagnosis is right that the capability guard was certified on the WRONG vector (line 260 checks a [:500] slice of the compartment LABEL list while lines 262-268 permute cytf) and right that the stored dict {capable, changed, reason} lacks the achievable/threshold keys every branch of the current gate_guard emits, i.e. pre-loop-119 code. But it missed the bigger fault: Q4's gate window is [100, 400] mg/mL and the null distribution's entire +/-4sd span is 105.3-147.9 -- INSIDE the window. All 20 shuffles pass Q4. The loop's headline 'the crowding ceiling is reached with the missing protein' is a gate a random permutation of the pool fractions clears. By gate_guard's own docstring ('a gate that cannot pass is the same fault as a null that cannot move'), the mirror case belongs in the same family and is unrecorded.

6. SECOND NUMERICAL ERROR. The diagnosis says Q3's measurement arm is scored on 'the cleanly organellar ~28% of mass'. Summing the mappable categories from the loop's own q5.whole gives 16.2% (13.4% post-split); 28.8% is the post-split Large Protein Complex share, mis-transcribed. The error runs against the diagnosis's own case -- the real figure makes Q3 worse.

7. WHAT I CONCEDE. Every structural finding stands and I verified each: grep over all 321 lines for pulse|oscill|cell.?cycle|NB4|elutriat|Ly et al|phase|amplitude returns nothing; n_positive = n_negative = 0; ITZ_TO_GEM maps 5 of 13 keys to None with no 'Cytosol' key at all (source lines 103-108); Q3's arms use unmatched, non-paired denominators 5,917 vs 23,225, so the manifest control 'annotation and measurement scored against the same GEM reactions' is false as written; 'Q5 dual localisation quantified' is a hardcoded True (line 284); q6 = bool(cap['capable']) discards pubs_rho (line 276); 'coverage by MASS' is literally X/X (line 273). The loop is genuine infrastructure repair for loops 92/102/116 and is internally coherent with its own docstring -- it simply never poses the oscillation question. My objection is only to which defect is named primary.

8. HONESTY ON THE SELF-FLATTERING AXIS. wrong-property is self-flattering too, and I will not overclaim it. The data CANNOT distinguish wrong-property from genuinely-absent for the KINETIC mechanism, because no time-resolved organellar map has ever been run in this repo -- a static null cannot refute a kinetic claim. What I can say: the static proxy is now tested and null at adequate power, and the mechanism carries an unrepaired specification gap the diagnosis noted in prose but never let drive its classification -- relocalisation is mass-conserving and Ly et al. measure whole-cell lysate LFQ, so a compartment swap cannot produce an abundance oscillation at all without an unstated coupling (localisation gating degradation, or compartment-dependent extraction efficiency). A mechanism whose proposed property has no specified path to the measured observable is a property defect, not a population defect. That is the third independent route to the same conclusion.

the_two_independent_reasons.the_distinction: BOTH hold, they are independent, and they are NOT equally load-bearing. The 5'UTR null is narrower: it rules out static cis-architecture as the discriminator, but cannot rule out trans-acting translational control. So the mechanism CLASS is genuinely excluded by arithmetic; the specific cis-signature tested is genuinely absent. The instrument was NOT bad -- it was answering a narrower question than the headline 'k_sp(t) translation NO SIGNAL' implies.

130.fair_test_would_need: 1) A different endpoint: the Ly 2014 NB4 protein oscillator set itself, not HPA CCD-transcript calls, and protein amplitude as a graded target rather than a binary. 2) A non-degenerate instrument: per-TF measured activity phase and amplitude (a real cell-cycle TF activity waveform, e.g. from the CCD-transcript time course of each regulator) instead of one shared sine on a static binary CCD-protein flag, so that timing rather than regulator count carries the signal, and so that the 62.3% of genes currently pinned at exactly zero get a graded score. 3) An OUTPUT-side capability check: extend gate_guard to assert the null moves the STATISTIC (e.g. require rank correlation between real and nulled scores below some bound), not merely the input vector -- the 87/13 sign skew makes the current check pass vacuously. 4) Degree-matched scoring by construction (sample null networks with identical in-degree and identical CCD-regulator count) rather than post-hoc quintile stratification on n = 239. 5) Power: 64 CCD-protein regulators out of 1,165 is too few for a within-decile permutation null; the null SD of 0.0734 against a real effect of 0.1404 caps |z| near 1.9 even if the effect were perfectly clean. 6) Most importantly, restrict the claim: because tanh(b*T/4) excludes production for 68.8% of oscillators, any TF-network test should be scored ONLY on the 25 of 80 genes that sit UNDER the ceiling, where a production mechanism is still admissible. Run on the whole set it is arithmetically guaranteed to fail regardless of the network.
