# POWER AND DILUTION — what the Ly-2014 sample sizes can and cannot see

Simulated, not tabulated. Scripts:
`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cell/0f039315-b3a9-52ac-8187-9fae0d726994/scratchpad/power_dilution.py`
(+ `sens.py`, `sens2.py`); raw log in `power_out.txt`. 4,000–12,000 sims per point, seeded,
two-sided, alpha 0.01, power target 0.80. Empirical type-I error was checked at every design
point and came back 0.0080–0.0110 against a nominal 0.0100, so the tests are calibrated.

## SETUP — the actual split

Ly et al. 2014, `ly2014_supp1-v1.txt`, all six `LFQ_intensity_F1..F6 > 0` and `gene_names`
present: **6,470 rows, 6,372 unique genes**. Phases G1=mean(F1,F2), S=mean(F3,F4),
G2=mean(F5,F6); oscillating at max/min >= 2.0.

| set | n_osc | n_flat | osc rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FULL** — all quantified genes | **209** | **6,163** | 3.28% |
| **W2SUB** — D-box carriers only (the set loop 153's W2 actually tested) | **104** | **2,717** | — |

The ELM `DEG_APCC_DBOX_1` regex `.R..L..[LIVM].` hits 8,904/20,213 = 44.1% of the proteome,
reproducing loop 153's promiscuity number. I report both row sets throughout because W2 was run
on the smaller one and that is where the real limit bites.

## 1. MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT — continuous feature (Mann-Whitney)

| set | n1 / n0 | type-I @ d=0 | min detectable d | **AUC threshold** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 209 / 6,163 | 0.0103 | 0.246 SD | **0.569** |
| W2SUB | 104 / 2,717 | 0.0110 | 0.351 SD | **0.598** |

Simulated AUCs matched the analytic Φ(d/√2) to within 0.0002, so the ranks are behaving.

**The W2 gate was set at AUC >= 0.60 and the detection floor on that set is 0.598.** The repo's
own pass gate sits essentially exactly at the smallest effect the experiment can resolve — there
is no margin at all between "detectable" and "declared real."

## 2. MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT — binary feature (chi-square, Fisher-confirmed)

Fisher-exact power at the chi-square-derived delta is in parentheses; the two agree to ~0.02–0.05,
so the fast test is not flattering itself.

| p0 | FULL: min Δ | → p1 | OR | (Fisher pw) | W2SUB: min Δ | → p1 | OR | (Fisher pw) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 0.060 | 0.110 | 2.34 | (0.76) | **0.088** | 0.138 | 3.04 | (0.73) |
| 0.20 | 0.101 | 0.301 | 1.72 | (0.78) | **0.144** | 0.344 | 2.09 | (0.78) |
| 0.44 | 0.120 | 0.560 | 1.62 | (0.78) | **0.168** | 0.608 | 1.98 | (0.77) |
| 0.69 | 0.108 | 0.798 | 1.78 | (0.80) | **0.149** | 0.839 | 2.34 | (0.81) |

**How promiscuity degrades detectability.** On raw Δ the answer is non-monotone (worst at 0.44,
where binomial variance peaks) and that framing is misleading. The honest quantity is Δ_required
as a fraction of the **headroom** left, (1 − p0):

| p0 | headroom 1−p0 | W2SUB Δ required | **fraction of all remaining headroom you must consume** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.088 | 9.3% |
| 0.20 | 0.80 | 0.144 | 17.9% |
| 0.44 | 0.56 | 0.168 | 30.1% |
| 0.69 | 0.31 | 0.149 | **48.1%** |

A degron already carried by 69% of the background must be carried by 84% of the oscillators — it
has to eat half of everything left — before this experiment can see it. That is the quantitative
form of Lu's point that a motif in two-thirds of the proteome cannot separate anything.

Compounded with dilution it is worse. If a **perfectly penetrant** degron (100% of the true
subgroup carries it) is present in fraction f of the positives, the observed prevalence lift is
only f·(1−p0). Minimum f for 80% power, even at perfect penetrance:

| p0 | FULL f_min | W2SUB f_min | power at f = 0.173 (W2SUB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 0.061 | 0.091 | 0.997 |
| 0.20 | 0.123 | 0.181 | 0.765 |
| 0.44 | 0.305 | 0.305 | **0.263** |
| 0.69 | 0.346 | 0.475 | **0.064** |

At the repo's own 44% D-box prevalence and a 17.3%-APC positive set, a **flawless** binary degron
has a 26% chance of being detected. At 69% it has a 6% chance. The presence tests were not
underpowered by accident; they were arithmetically incapable.

## 3. THE DILUTION CURVE

Positives: fraction f drawn from the shifted law, the remaining (1−f) drawn from the *same* law as
the flats. Simulated observed AUC on the whole positive set vs the whole flat set.

**FULL (209 vs 6,163), threshold AUC 0.569:**

| AUC_true | f | observed AUC | sd | ≥0.60? | ≥thr (0.569)? | power @ α .01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.75 | 0.05 | 0.5125 | 0.021 | no | no | 0.025 |
| 0.75 | 0.10 | 0.5251 | 0.021 | no | no | 0.090 |
| 0.75 | **0.17** | **0.5426** | 0.021 | no | no | **0.320** |
| 0.75 | 0.25 | 0.5626 | 0.021 | no | no | 0.690 |
| 0.75 | 0.50 | 0.6253 | 0.021 | YES | YES | 1.000 |
| 0.75 | 1.00 | 0.7500 | 0.017 | YES | YES | 1.000 |
| 0.85 | 0.05 | 0.5176 | 0.021 | no | no | 0.047 |
| 0.85 | 0.10 | 0.5352 | 0.021 | no | no | 0.215 |
| 0.85 | **0.17** | **0.5596** | 0.022 | no | no | **0.637** |
| 0.85 | 0.25 | 0.5876 | 0.022 | no | YES | 0.947 |
| 0.85 | 0.50 | 0.6754 | 0.021 | YES | YES | 1.000 |
| 0.85 | 1.00 | 0.8500 | 0.013 | YES | YES | 1.000 |

**W2SUB (104 vs 2,717), threshold AUC 0.598:**

| AUC_true | f | observed AUC | sd | ≥0.60? | ≥thr (0.598)? | power @ α .01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.75 | 0.05 | 0.5123 | 0.029 | no | no | 0.017 |
| 0.75 | 0.10 | 0.5248 | 0.029 | no | no | 0.043 |
| 0.75 | **0.17** | **0.5423** | 0.029 | no | no | **0.138** |
| 0.75 | 0.25 | 0.5623 | 0.029 | no | no | 0.344 |
| 0.75 | 0.50 | 0.6247 | 0.029 | YES | YES | 0.960 |
| 0.75 | 1.00 | 0.7497 | 0.024 | YES | YES | 1.000 |
| 0.85 | 0.05 | 0.5174 | 0.029 | no | no | 0.027 |
| 0.85 | 0.10 | 0.5349 | 0.029 | no | no | 0.091 |
| 0.85 | **0.17** | **0.5593** | 0.030 | no | no | **0.306** |
| 0.85 | 0.25 | 0.5873 | 0.030 | no | no | 0.669 |
| 0.85 | 0.50 | 0.6747 | 0.029 | YES | YES | 0.999 |
| 0.85 | 1.00 | 0.8499 | 0.019 | YES | YES | 1.000 |

Dilution is exactly linear in the AUC metric — simulated values track
`AUC_obs = f·AUC_true + (1−f)·0.5` to within 0.0006 everywhere. That is the whole story in one
line: **AUC is an average over the positive set, and averaging a strong minority against an
inert majority is straight linear attenuation.** A no-margin gate of 0.60 on a diluted set is a
gate on f, not on the mechanism.

## 4. THE SMALLEST USABLE f

| set | AUC_true | f_min for 80% power | f needed to clear the repo's AUC ≥ 0.60 gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 0.85 | **0.203** | 0.286 |
| FULL | 0.75 | 0.283 | 0.400 |
| W2SUB | 0.85 | **0.285** | 0.286 |
| W2SUB | 0.75 | 0.398 | 0.400 |

**A real, strong (AUC 0.85) mechanism needs to cover ~20% of the positives on the full set and
~29% on the D-box subset before this experiment can see it at all.**

**What that means for a positive set that is 17.3% APC substrates:** 17.3% is *below* both floors.
On the set W2 actually used, a true within-subgroup AUC of 0.85 — a genuinely strong, mechanistic,
correct hypothesis — yields observed AUC 0.559 and is detected **31% of the time**. At AUC_true
0.75, 14%. In other words the W2 test, as run, would have missed a real APC-processivity effect
roughly 7 times out of 10 in the best case and 6 times out of 7 in the plausible case. **W2's
failure carries almost no evidence against the hypothesis.** It is not a tenth elimination; it is
a non-result. The honest verdict on a f=0.173 positive set is *underpowered*, and the correct
next move is to test the 18 known APC substrates as their own positive set rather than to test
the 104 and call the null an answer.

## 5. SANITY ANCHOR — the measured +6.5%

Recomputed from the FASTA and the ELM regex, reproducing loop 153 exactly:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| lysines within 60 of best D-box, oscillators | 8.404 (n=104) |
| lysines, flat | 7.894 (n=2,717) |
| enrichment | **+6.46%** |
| pooled SD | 4.140 |
| Cohen's d | 0.1233 |
| **observed AUC (rank, measured)** | **0.5381** — matches loop 153's `auc_raw` 0.5381 |
| observed AUC implied by +6.5% under a normal model | 0.5347 |
| Mann-Whitney two-sided p | 0.185 |

**f required for that observation to reflect a true within-subgroup AUC of 0.75:
f = (0.5381 − 0.5)/0.25 = 0.153, i.e. 15.3% of the oscillators.** (At AUC_true 0.85, f = 0.109.)

The independently-measured APC fraction of that set is **17.3%**. Simulating f = 0.173 with
AUC_true = 0.75 on 104 vs 2,717 gives observed AUC 0.5432 ± 0.0295 — the measured 0.5381 sits
**0.17 sd away**. Inverting instead: at f = 0.173 the within-subgroup AUC needed to produce the
observed 0.5381 is **0.720**.

So the +6.5% is quantitatively consistent with a real, respectable-strength lysine-proximity
effect (AUC ≈ 0.72–0.75) carried by the ~17% of oscillators that are APC substrates, and
completely inconsistent with the effect being absent. It is also, at these n, indistinguishable
from zero — p = 0.185. **Both readings are supported by the same number. That is the definition
of an underpowered design, and it is the finding.**

## WHERE THE ANSWER IS SENSITIVE TO AN ASSUMPTION

1. **The non-mechanism oscillators are assumed to be distributed exactly like the flats.** This is
   the load-bearing assumption and it is optimistic in one direction and pessimistic in the other.
   Simulated at f=0.173, AUC_true=0.85, W2SUB: a +0.05 SD nuisance shift in the other 83%
   (length/abundance confounding, say) lifts observed AUC 0.559 → 0.572 and power 0.33 → 0.48; a
   +0.10 SD shift gives 0.584 and power 0.64; a −0.05 SD shift gives 0.549 and power 0.20. A mild
   confound moves power by a factor of two. Loop 153's ρ(score, length) = 0.246 says such a shift
   is not hypothetical.
2. **Which n you use.** FULL (209/6,163) vs W2SUB (104/2,717) moves the AUC floor 0.569 → 0.598
   and f_min@0.85 from 0.203 → 0.285. Restricting to D-box carriers cost ~40% of the effective
   sample. Every "how bad is it" number depends on this choice; I report both.
3. **Alpha and sidedness.** Two-sided α .01 is what the repo declared. One-sided α .01 →
   threshold 0.590 (W2SUB); α .05 → 0.580; α .001 (a plausible correction for ten tested
   mechanisms) → **0.618**, pushing f_min@AUC_true 0.85 to 0.337. Multiple-testing correction
   across the ten mechanisms makes the dilution problem strictly worse, and the ten-way search is
   already in the record.
4. **Normal shift as the model of the effect.** AUC_true is specified directly and the mixture
   linearity `AUC_obs = f·AUC_true + (1−f)·0.5` is distribution-free, so steps 3–4 barely depend
   on this. Step 5's two AUC estimates do: the rank AUC of the real lysine counts is 0.5381 while
   the normal model implied by +6.5% gives 0.5347, because lysine counts are right-skewed and
   discrete. The gap (0.003) is small relative to the 0.030 sampling sd, so it changes no
   conclusion, but the mean-enrichment → AUC conversion is not exact for this feature.
5. **AUC_true = 0.75/0.85 is stipulated, not measured.** Loop 153's W0 measured +50.6% mean
   lysine enrichment on Lu's published substrate set, which is a mean ratio, not an AUC; mapping
   it to a within-subgroup AUC requires the same skewed-distribution assumption as (4). The
   inverted number in step 5 (AUC_true ≈ 0.72 at f = 0.173) is the version that does not need
   that stipulation, and it is the one I would quote.
